Company Description
With over $2B in revenue, 80+ manufacturing facilities across 6 continents and over 9,000 employees worldwide, Signode is a leading manufacturer of a broad spectrum of transit packaging consumables, tools, software, and equipment that optimize end-of-line packaging operations and protect products in transit. Signode brings this extensive product portfolio together under hundreds of trusted brands to offer complete transit packaging solutions to its customers.
We produce strap, stretch and protective packaging. We also manufacture packaging tools and equipment used to apply the bulk packaging materials. These commercial packaging products are used to pack, bundle, unitize, protect, and secure goods during warehousing and transit. Our company is a pioneer in the industrial packaging sector with a long history of customer-focused innovations in materials, processes and automation technology that have revolutionized the sector.
Headquartered in Tampa, Florida, we are proud to be the Transit Packaging Division of Crown Holdings, Inc. We are excited to go to market as Signode and to share the portfolio of products, services and capabilities that make us the world’s premier end-of-line packaging company.
Job Description
Benefits:
Signode offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees, which includes health, dental, vision, 401k, paid time off, life insurance, wellness perks, and more. Benefits begin the month following the hire date.
Summary
This role is for a Plant Manager who is a true leader, one who can build a strong, positive culture throughout the plant. The position calls for a sharp operational and analytical mind that constantly seeks out, teaches, and leads improvements in Safety Performance, Cost Control, Standardized Processes (LEAN), Production Reporting, and Inventory Control.
This is a high-visibility opportunity to lead one of Signode’s most important locations, having a big impact on our ability to deliver a profitable year. Here is what makes this role stand out:
- Pilot the company’s Operational Excellence system, delivering a glidepath in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Output, and Morale.
- Take charge of a major turnaround facility. The right leader is confident yet humble, ready to run a 24/7 site from the bottom up, and understands the sweat and equity required to turn it around.
- Succeed here, and fast-track your path to the next level.
Essential Functions
- Directly manage and coordinate the activities of various plant departments and sites within Signode. 
- Provide strong leadership to the manufacturing team, fostering a collaborative and results-oriented work environment. 
- Develop and implement strategic plans to achieve production goals, optimize processes, and enhance overall plant efficiency. 
- Communicate, uphold and enforce safety protocols and regulatory compliance to maintain a safe and secure working environment. 
- Responsible for talent management and employee lifecycle activities, from hiring to terminating.
- Collaborate with senior management to align plant operations with organizational objectives. 
- Monitor and analyze production metrics, ensuring that production targets are met while maintaining high-quality standards. 
- Implement efficiency improvement initiatives and address any bottlenecks or issues in the production process. 
- Efficiently allocate resources, including manpower and equipment, to meet production schedules and deadlines. 
- Collaborate with the maintenance team to ensure optimal functionality of machinery and equipment. 
- Collaborate with the quality control department to ensure that products meet or exceed quality standards. 
- Implement measures to address any deviations or non-conformities in the production process. 
- Develop and manage budgets for the manufacturing facility(s), controlling costs and optimizing resource utilization. 
- Identify cost-saving opportunities and implement measures to improve overall plant profitability. 
- Effectively communicate with senior management, department heads, and front-line staff to ensure clear understanding of goals and objectives. 
- Prepare regular reports on plant performance, production metrics, and other relevant KPIs. 
- Lead and support initiatives for continuous improvement, identifying opportunities to enhance plant processes, reduce waste, and increase overall efficiency. 
Qualifications
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Management, Business, or Engineering. Masters Degree in similar field preferred.
Experience: Minimum of 15+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, with at least 5 -7 years in a managerial or supervisory role. Previous experience as a plant manager is a must.
- Financial Acumen with the ability to analyze and forecast data and translate results to better solutions.  With the understanding of general ledger accounting and activity rate costing.
- Strong knowledge of safety metrics and programs.
- TPM mastery
- Previous experience leading a turnaround factory
- Extrusion technical skills
- ERP system knowledge a plus.
- LEAN Manufacturing Training or CI Management Experience (Tier I, II, III)
Functional Success Drivers: These competencies are what we require for an individual to be successful in this role.
- Strategic Skills
- Leadership
- Result Oriented
- Safety & Security
- Communication (Oral & Written)
- Analytical Skills
- Inspiring “Followership”
- Vision

The Company does not sponsor for employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

Premise Health serves large organizations and their people with exceptional healthcare. The result? Better experiences, better health, and better value, all while helping organizations lower their healthcare costs.

This position oversees and directs the operations management of multiple employer worksites across all lines of health and fitness related services within a geographic area. The Director of Client Operations is a subject matter expert and provides expertise managing and mentoring Health Center Leadership staff.
This is a full time, remote Director of Client Operations role supporting our East region.

- Strategically identifies and solves complex problems effectively with an emphasis on developing proactive approaches utilizing internal (corporate and regional) support.
- Identifies and requests participation from corporate departments in strategic meetings as client needs dictate.
- Owns client/site meetings, committees, and task forces to support strategic initiatives and goals.
- Operational lead on implementations post-go-live.
- Coordinates and productively facilitates communication across virtual sites and effectively navigates through multilayer client relationships (vendors, consultants, etc).

- Provides effective leadership, coaching, and mentoring at the site level.
- Builds talent to proactively manage additional LOS.
- Participates in sales process.
- Escalation point for clients.
- Consults with Medical, Legal or Compliance departments regarding regulations, practices act, practice law, certification requirements etc.
- May be asked to complete ad hoc projects.
- Manages site level supervisors.
- Owns the client/site meetings, committees and task forces to support strategic initiative and goals; identifies and asks for participation of corporate departments in strategic meetings as client needs dictate.
- Coordinates and communicates across virtual sites and shares best demonstrated practices with peers.
- May be asked to complete ad hoc projects.
- Oversees the management of up to 15 health centers with multiple lines of service.
- Manages the relationship of up to 10 clients.
- Manages a portfolio of $2M - $10M in Gross Annual Revenue

- 10+ years’ experience in a business environment or related industry, managing others
- Experience managing virtual teams

- Demonstrated process or efficiency management.

- Excellent demonstrated follow up skills & attention to detail
- Ability to work both independently and as a team member
- Strong relationship building skills
- Ability to interact at all levels of the organization (both internal and external)
- Demonstrated strong leadership skills
- Demonstrated adaptability and ability to manage change

Head of Network Quality
About Aeris Communications Inc.
Aeris is the secure connectivity platform for Physical AI and intelligent IoT devices. It caters to connected cars, drones, autonomous mobility, robotics, utilities, energy, fleet management, logistics, medical devices, and manufacturing. Aeris serves over 7,000 enterprise customers and connects more than 115 million devices worldwide, including 41 million connected vehicles, supported by an ecosystem of 30+ mobile network operators. Enterprises rely on Aeris for the borderless connectivity, embedded security, observability, and proven scale that mission critical Physical AI programs demand.
Role Overview
Aeris is hiring a Head of Network Quality to build and own a new function responsible for network quality governance, test lab operations, and automated validation across our IP/Cellular network supporting more than 100M devices worldwide. This leader will establish standardized quality frameworks, embed quality controls into engineering and change processes, and leverage AI-driven automation to reduce outages and protect SLAs.
This is an opportunity to shape how quality is engineered into a global cellular network from the ground up. You’ll define the systems, standards, and automation capabilities that improve network stability and release confidence while partnering across Engineering, Operations, Architecture, and Quality teams. Based in Chicago or Bucharest, this role reports to Claudio Taglienti and offers direct visibility into senior engineering leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Network Quality Governance

- Establish quality metrics and reporting to measure validation effectiveness, compliance, automation coverage, and customer-impacting issues.

Test Lab & Validation Frameworks
- Build and lead a managed Network Test Lab supporting consistent pre-production validation.
- Develop validation workflows and scalable regression testing capabilities across the Aeris network environment.
- Create structured, repeatable approaches to validating network designs and changes before production deployment.
Automation & AI Enablement
- Develop automated validation and regression testing capabilities that reduce reliance on manual testing.
- Leverage AI and agentic automation approaches to improve regression testing and engineer compliance validation.
- Identify opportunities to automate operational quality processes with measurable business impact.
Cross-Functional Leadership
- Partner across Network Engineering, Operations, Architecture, and Quality teams to improve network reliability and operational consistency.
- Guide technical decision-making around network quality standards, feasibility, and implementation priorities.

The Director, Franchise Business Consultant and Operations is a hands-on leader of consultants that are the primary contact between the franchisor and the franchisee. You and your team members will act as the franchisee’s connection to the Franchise Support Center ensuring there is a strong support system and trusted advisors in place. This position will oversee operational KPI’s for the region and team, ensuring they are providing management, operational, and financial support to franchise partners through a consultative relationship built on trust. The strength of that relationship will directly impact your team’s ability to be an effective FBC. You are the leader of coaches, advising how franchisees should leverage our Systems of Business in the effort to help them reach their personal and business goals.
Responsibilities
- Lead a regional team of franchise business consultants in support of our franchisee’s growth and aspirations.
- Perform the role of business consultant and coach; building trust with your team as well as your franchise partners to influence growth and profitability within their franchise
- Be the go-to person for your leadership for any and all information as it pertains to your region.
- Establish a regular cadence of virtual and onsite touch points to maintain a deep understanding of the business operations of our franchise partners, providing insights and assistance when needed
- Develop a deep understanding of all available Authority Brand tools, platforms, and support systems available to our brands to maximize performance and instill trust with your franchisees
- Coach your team to be the person your franchisees seek out for advice, come to in a time of crisis, or to celebrate the victories they have experienced
- Prioritize the requests of the FSC functions to connect with your franchisees
- Advise our franchise partners on the importance of staying in compliance with the Franchise Agreement and assisting when needed in the efforts to help the franchise partner stay compliant
- Conduct market meetings for your franchisees, bringing groups of franchisees together for the betterment of the group
- Providing guidance to the franchisees in the development of their culture and how it acts as an extension of our company culture
- Responsible for delivering franchisee territory ‘health’ diagnostics
- Performing a monthly Profit and Loss statement reviews including YOY revenue
- Other duties as assigned 
Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree (B.A) or Equivalent experience required
- 6 - 8+ years of experience in the capacity of a consultant, advisor, coach, or in running a services-based business or franchise
- Managerial and/or team leader experience
- Skilled in operational efficiencies, best practices, KPI’s, and data analysis
- Comfortable interpreting P&L statements and understanding how various initiatives may impact top & bottom lines
- Experience partnering cross functionally to ensure your customers get what they need when they need it
- Skilled in communicating clearly and motivating those around you
- Ability to travel up to 75% to Franchisee locations within your assigned territory

[Structured job data] title: Senior Manager, Protective Operations | employer: Crusoe | baseSalary: none | validThrough: None
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.
We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.
We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.
If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.
About the Role:
Crusoe is building the infrastructure that powers the AI revolution. As our global footprint expands across data centers, power generation, manufacturing, construction sites, and corporate offices — and as the visibility of our executives and the stakes of our operations continue to rise — the ability to protect our people wherever the business takes them is increasingly critical.
The Senior Manager, Protective Operations will lead Crusoe's executive protection and protective operations programs globally, providing risk-based protection for executives, employees, travelers, and company operations. You will serve as the company's subject matter expert for executive protection, travel risk, protective intelligence, threat management, and sensitive security investigations.
This role will join Crusoe's growing Physical Security organization at a formative moment. You will shape the standards, protocols, vendor network, and operating rhythm that supports Crusoe's expanding global footprint — working closely with the GSOC, the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst, People, Legal, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, and business leaders to identify risk and translate intelligence into effective protective measures.
The ideal candidate brings experience from U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, high-end executive protection, special operations, or protective details at the national or diplomatic level, and has translated that tradecraft into corporate Protective Operations leadership. You know how to protect people without unnecessarily disrupting the business, and you know how to lead a program that scales.
What You'll Be Working On:
Executive Protection Program Leadership
- 
Lead Crusoe's global Executive Protection program, including executive travel, residential considerations, ground transportation, advance work, event coverage, and protective operations
- 
Develop risk-based protection strategies based on threat, exposure, location, activity, and other relevant factors rather than title alone
- 
Lead security planning for executive appearances, media engagements, conferences, town halls, board activities, major company events, and other high-profile engagements
- 
Establish and maintain the standards, protocols, and tradecraft discipline expected of a world-class corporate protection program
Travel Risk Management
- 
Own the Travel Risk Management program, establishing processes for pre-travel risk assessment, traveler briefings, high-risk travel, escalation, emergency support, and traveler assistance
- 
Conduct advance work and security assessments for domestic and international travel, including hotels, venues, transportation, routes, medical capabilities, and contingency planning
- 
Build the duty-of-care framework and escalation procedures that protect Crusoe travelers wherever the business sends them
Protective Intelligence Partnership
- 
Partner closely with the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst and the GSOC to translate protective intelligence into protective action — movement planning, principal protection decisions, advance planning, and threat response
- 
Shape the intelligence requirements and collection priorities that support protective operations
- 
Operationalize protective intelligence products into daily decisions, travel decisions, and event planning
Threat Assessment and Management
- 
Establish and support threat assessment and management processes for workplace violence, threatening communications, stalking, harassment, fixated individuals, concerning behavior, and other potential threats
- 
Partner with HR, Employee Relations, Legal, and the Intelligence Analyst on threat cases requiring coordinated response and protective action
- 
Apply structured behavioral threat assessment methodologies to differentiate legitimate threats from noise
Sensitive Security Investigations
- 
Lead or support sensitive security investigations involving threats, theft, misconduct, unauthorized access, insider risk, security incidents, and suspected fraud in partnership with Legal, People, Internal Audit, Information Security, and other stakeholders
- 
Support elevated-risk employee matters, including sensitive terminations, credible threats, domestic violence concerns affecting the workplace, and other situations requiring additional protective measures
- 
Maintain investigative discipline, chain of custody, and reporting standards appropriate to the sensitivity of each matter
Site and Geographic Risk Assessment
- 
Conduct geographic and site security risk assessments in support of new markets, potential company locations, major projects, and business expansion
- 
Evaluate country, city, neighborhood, and site-level risks including crime, political instability, civil unrest, terrorism, emergency response, medical capabilities, transportation, natural hazards, and other relevant threats
- 
Produce assessments that inform executive travel, site selection, event planning, and business expansion decisions
Program Development and Vendor Management
- 
Develop protective operations plans, standards, protocols, and escalation procedures that scale across a growing global organization
- 
Select, manage, and evaluate executive protection, secure transportation, travel security, investigative, and other specialized security vendors globally
- 
Grow the vendor network — domestic and international — required to extend Crusoe's protective capabilities wherever the business operates
- 
Support budget development, forecasting, and financial management for protective operations programs and vendors
Operational Partnership
- 
Coordinate closely with the GSOC during executive travel, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents
- 
Establish relationships with law enforcement, government agencies, security partners, and other external organizations relevant to protective operations
- 
Support crisis and incident response involving executives, employees, travelers, threats, or other security events
Program Measurement and Maturity
- 
Develop metrics and reporting to measure program effectiveness, emerging risks, protective activity, and opportunities for improvement
- 
Help mature the Protective Operations function as Crusoe's global footprint and risk profile continue to evolve
- 
Maintain discretion and sound judgment when handling highly sensitive executive, employee, investigative, and company information
What You'll Bring to the Team:
- 
10+ years of experience in executive protection, corporate security, protective intelligence, law enforcement, military protective operations, diplomatic security, or a related field
- 
5+ years leading complex executive protection, protective operations, or corporate security programs
- 
Demonstrated experience protecting senior executives and supporting domestic and international travel
- 
Strong experience conducting advances, threat assessments, security risk assessments, and protective planning
- 
Experience developing and managing executive protection programs in a corporate environment strongly preferred
- 
Knowledge of protective intelligence, behavioral threat assessment, workplace violence prevention, and threat management principles
- 
Experience conducting or managing sensitive corporate or security investigations
- 
Understanding of travel risk management, including international security environments, traveler risk assessment, emergency response, and duty-of-care considerations
- 
Experience planning security for media engagements, executive appearances, major events, and other high-profile activities
- 
Ability to assess rapidly evolving situations, make sound risk-based decisions, and operate effectively with incomplete information
- 
Demonstrated ability to work with senior executives while maintaining discretion, professionalism, adaptability, and confidentiality
- 
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate risk and recommendations to executives and business leaders
- 
Experience managing specialized security vendors, executive protection providers, secure transportation providers, and other external partners
- 
Ability to collaborate effectively across Legal, People, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, Operations, and other business functions
- 
Ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 30–50%, with periods of increased travel based on operational requirements
- 
Ability to respond outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support
Bonus Points
- 
Prior service with U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, FBI, DEA, U.S. Marshals Service, or an equivalent federal protective agency
- 
Military special operations background with protective detail experience (SOF, MARSOC, Naval Special Warfare, Air Force Special Tactics, or equivalent)
- 
Prior corporate executive protection leadership experience within technology, critical infrastructure, data centers, energy, manufacturing, or another rapidly growing global organization
- 
Experience leading principal-level protective details for Fortune 500 CEOs, founders, or high-net-worth principals
- 
Experience developing enterprise Travel Risk Management or Workplace Violence Prevention programs
- 
Experience conducting protective intelligence and open-source threat research
- 
Experience supporting international operations and higher-risk travel environments, including gray and amber travel zones
- 
Experience working with law enforcement, intelligence, diplomatic, or government security organizations
- 
Familiarity with intelligence, case management, mass notification, travel risk, and security operations platforms (Ontic, Dataminr, Everbridge, International SOS, Crisis24, or peer tools)
- 
CPP, PSP, PCI, Certified Threat Manager (CTM), ATAP certifications, or other relevant professional credentials
- 
Multilingual capability, particularly in languages supporting Crusoe's international footprint
Operating Conditions:
- 
San Francisco or Denver on-site, with domestic and international travel of approximately 30–50% to support executive protection, advance work, high-risk travel, site assessments, and major events
- 
On-call availability for executive travel windows, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents
- 
Response outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support
- 
Occasional nights, weekends, and holidays as the operational tempo demands
- 
Handling of sensitive, confidential, and executive-protection information with appropriate discretion is a core expectation of the role
What Success Looks Like:
Success in this role means Crusoe has a proactive, intelligence-led, and risk-based protective operations program capable of supporting executives and employees wherever the business operates.
You will lead a program that identifies threats early, provides executives and travelers with appropriate protection without unnecessarily disrupting business, responds effectively to sensitive incidents, and scales as Crusoe expands into new markets and operating environments.
You will also establish a close operating partnership with the GSOC and the Intelligence Analyst: the GSOC maintains global situational awareness and enterprise threat monitoring, the Intelligence Analyst produces protective intelligence assessments, and Protective Operations owns the translation of intelligence into protective action.
Benefits:
- 
Competitive compensation and equity packages
- 
Restricted Stock Units
- 
Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs
- 
Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance
- 
Employer contributions to HSA account
- 
Paid parental leave
- 
Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability
- 
Professional development & tuition reimbursement
- 
Mental health & wellness support
- 
Commuter benefits (parking & transit)
- 
Cell phone stipend
- 
401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary
- 
Volunteer time off
- 
Global travel insurance & emergency assistance
- 
Daily meals allowance
- 
Additional perks & programs specific to location
Compensation Range
Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

 Your Next Chapter. Our Newest Community.
Imagine welcoming the first Residents to a community you helped bring to life—knowing your leadership helped prepare the buildings, develop the team, and put the details in place for a successful opening.
Fleet Landing at Nocatee is seeking a Director of Campus Operations to lead Interior and Exterior Maintenance, Housekeeping, and Safety and Security. This is an opportunity to help launch a new community, establish operational standards, and build a team whose work makes a difference in Residents’ daily lives.
We’re looking for a leader who sees both the big picture and the details: someone who can work effectively with a construction team, coach department leaders, and ensure every Resident arrives at a home that is ready to welcome them.
Our Story
Fleet Landing’s story began in 1990 with a commitment to helping older adults live well through exceptional service, meaningful relationships, and a welcoming community. Fleet Landing at Nocatee, our new Life Plan Community, will carry that commitment forward.
As a member of the opening leadership team, you’ll help shape how the community operates from day one—building the relationships, service standards, and daily practices that will support Residents and staff for years to come.
What You’ll Do
Help bring the community from construction to operation.
- Partner with the construction team and community leaders to coordinate an efficient, effective handover of buildings, grounds, equipment, and systems. 
- Participate in walkthroughs, identify operational concerns, and follow through on punch-list items and construction deficiencies. 
- Ensure the operating team receives the training, maintenance information, warranties, and documentation needed to manage the community confidently. 
- Align operational readiness with construction milestones and Resident move-in schedules. 
Make move-in readiness a priority.
- Coordinate with Sales, Resident Services, construction partners, and department leaders to prepare Resident units for scheduled move-ins. 
- Establish readiness checklists and final inspections to confirm homes are clean, safe, functional, and welcoming. 
- Resolve outstanding issues promptly and communicate clearly when concerns could affect a Resident’s arrival. 
Build and lead a strong operations team.
- Recruit, develop, and support leaders and staff in Interior and Exterior Maintenance, Housekeeping, and Safety and Security. 
- Establish clear expectations, practical procedures, and a service culture grounded in responsiveness, accountability, and respect. 
- Create an environment where staff take pride in their work and understand how their contributions support the Resident experience. 
Deliver reliable, well-managed campus operations.
- Oversee preventive maintenance, repairs, housekeeping, grounds, and safety and security services. 
- Use WorxHub to manage work orders, maintenance schedules, equipment records, and service performance. 
- Manage operating and capital budgets, vendor relationships, and service agreements with attention to quality and responsible stewardship. 
- Maintain regulatory and survey readiness, support emergency preparedness, and address operational risks. 
- Work closely with the Executive Director and fellow leaders to improve service and support the community as occupancy grows. 
What You’ll Bring
- At least five years of operational experience at the administrative leadership level in a Continuing Care Retirement Community or equivalent setting. 
- Strong knowledge of facilities operations, building systems, preventive maintenance, safety, and regulatory requirements. 
- Demonstrated success managing projects, budgets, vendors, and multiple operational priorities. 
- A record of coaching staff, developing leaders, and building collaborative teams. 
- Clear communication, sound judgment, and the ability to follow through when details, deadlines, and competing needs demand attention. 
- A commitment to serving older adults and creating a positive experience for Residents and staff. 
- A bachelor’s degree is preferred, along with demonstrated success in facilities management, engineering, business administration, project management, financial management, or related areas. 
- Experience opening a new community or transitioning newly constructed facilities into operation is preferred. 
Why Fleet Landing
This role offers the opportunity to help build something lasting, supported by Fleet Landing’s established experience and commitment to excellence. You’ll have a meaningful voice in opening decisions, the opportunity to develop your team, and the satisfaction of seeing your work reflected throughout the community.
We offer competitive pay, comprehensive benefits, paid time off that begins accruing on day one, and a generous retirement plan—along with opportunities for continued learning and professional growth.
Bring your operational expertise, your leadership, and your commitment to service. Help us bring Fleet Landing at Nocatee to life.

**Position Summary**

Ham Farms is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead daily operations at our sweet potato dehydration plant in Farmville, North Carolina. The plant produces dehydrated sweet potato dog treats, and the Plant Manager is accountable for safety, product quality, food safety compliance, production output, cost control, and team development. This leader will run a safe, efficient, and consistent operation from raw sweet potato receiving through slicing, dehydration, packaging, and shipping.

**Key Responsibilities Operations and Production**

· Plan and direct daily production schedules to meet customer orders, yield targets, and delivery deadlines.

· Oversee receiving, washing, peeling, slicing, dehydration, cooling, packaging, and warehousing processes.

· Monitor dehydration time, temperature, and moisture levels to ensure consistent product texture and shelf stability.

· Track and improve key metrics such as yield, throughput, downtime, waste, and labor efficiency.

· Coordinate with farm operations and procurement on sweet potato supply, storage, and seasonal planning.

**Quality and Food Safety**

· Maintain compliance with FDA requirements, including FSMA and Current Good Manufacturing Practices for animal food, and with AAFCO and applicable state regulations.

· Lead the food safety plan, HACCP or preventive controls program, sanitation procedures, and allergen and pathogen controls.

· Prepare the plant for customer, third-party, and regulatory audits and close out corrective actions promptly.

· Manage lot tracking, traceability, and recall readiness.

People and Safety

· Recruit, train, schedule, coach, and supervise production, sanitation, maintenance, and warehouse staff.

· Promote a strong safety culture and ensure OSHA compliance, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, and forklift safety.

· Hold team members accountable to standards while building a respectful, engaged workforce.

**Equipment, Facilities, and Budget**

· Oversee preventive maintenance and repairs for dehydrators, slicers, conveyors, packaging lines, and utilities.

· Develop and manage the plant budget, labor plan, and capital requests.

· Manage inventory of raw materials, packaging, and finished goods.

· Lead continuous improvement and lean initiatives to lower cost and increase capacity.

**Qualifications Required**

· Bachelor’s degree in food science, agricultural or industrial engineering, operations management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

· 5 or more years of food, pet food, or agricultural manufacturing experience, including at least 2 years in a plant leadership or supervisory role.

· Working knowledge of FSMA, GMP, HACCP, and OSHA requirements.

· Demonstrated success managing production teams, budgets, and quality systems.

· Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office and production or inventory systems.

**Preferred**

· Experience with dehydration, drying, or thermal processing of fruits, vegetables, or pet treats.

· PCQI, HACCP, or SQF practitioner certification.

· Experience with lean manufacturing or Six Sigma methods.

· Familiarity with seasonal, farm-sourced raw materials.

Working Conditions

· Production environment with exposure to heat, moisture, noise, and cold storage areas.

· Ability to stand and walk for extended periods and lift up to 50 pounds.

· Must wear required PPE and follow all plant hygiene rules.

· Schedule may include extended hours, weekends, and seasonal peaks during harvest.

**Compensation and Benefits**

Compensation will be competitive and based on experience.

Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.

Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.

The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.

**Job Responsibilities:**
-------------------------

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).
* Builds the sector CI talent strategy: capability standards, certification pathways (e.g., ASCEND X, PME), succession planning, and rotation of high-potential leaders through CI roles.
* Coaches ESA executives on Lean leadership behaviors and role-models a culture of accountability and continuous improvement from the top.
* Sets sector maturity targets and owns the EBSA and OpA assessment strategy; reviews results with leadership and directs closure of systemic gaps.
* Represents ESA in enterprise CI forums; partners with Corporate CI & Quality to shape Eaton-wide standards and scale proven practices across sectors.
* Manages the ESA CI function budget and champions digital and data analytics tools that accelerate improvement.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

Required Qualifications: 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Quality, or Operations
* Minimum 5 years leading leaders (managers or directors) at a multi-site, division, or business-unit level
* Proven track record leading Lean transformations that delivered measurable financial results, preferably in a multi-division manufacturing environment
* Professional experience in a global matrixed organization
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc

Preferred Qualifications: 

* Master's degree or MBA preferred

Position Success Criteria: 

* Expert-level command of Lean and Six Sigma; Master Black Belt or Black Belt certification required
* Experience designing, governing, and maturing a business operating system and maturity model at scale
* Strong business and financial acumen: builds cost-out and productivity plans, quantifies impact, and ties CI results to the P&L
* Experience designing CI talent, certification, and capability programs across a large, multi-site organization
* Applies Lean to both manufacturing and office/transactional processes
* Executive presence; a trusted advisor who influences, challenges, and aligns senior executives
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams of senior CI leaders
* Strategic thinker who turns vision into multi-year roadmaps and leads change at scale
* Excellent communication at every level, from the shop floor to the executive leadership team

Manufacturing experience is a strong advantage, but exceptional organizational and operational leadership skills are the priority.

Strategic Production Planning & Scheduling

* Develop and maintain master production schedules across multiple custom projects.

* Translate project requirements and delivery commitments into actionable daily, weekly, and long-term plans.

* Coordinate labor, materials, equipment, and other resources to support production priorities.

* Anticipate scheduling conflicts, capacity limitations, and bottlenecks before they affect deadlines.

* Evaluate workflows and implement practical improvements to productivity and consistency.
